findings.title: baseline_mutual_surety
findings.claim: Membership entails mutual surety: people help carry one another's exposure and continuity as if bound by kinship.
findings.mechanism: The converging responsibility and surety branches recast the group as mutual liability. Members do not merely tell one another to endure; they stand with and answer for one another's capacity to endure, with kin-directed mercy naming whom that liability protects.
findings.reader_payoff: The communal profile becomes one of shared responsibility for another person's capacity to endure.

findings.title: baseline_generative_kinship
findings.claim: Mercy can be heard as the kin-like holding through which a secure community continually constitutes and receives its members.
findings.mechanism: The womb and kinship branches make mercy more than an emotion: it can be a generative holding environment. Reciprocal joining carries persons into a secure social body that produces belonging rather than merely recognizing a pre-existing identity.
findings.reader_payoff: Mercy becomes perceptible as a possible generative holding environment, not only a disposition displayed by an established group.
